claim: The aerial image of block after block of houses reduced to white ash while trees stand between them — presented as a signature of a beam weapon aimed at homes — is the Coffey Park neighborhood of Santa Rosa, California, photographed after the Tubbs Fire of October 2017. The Tubbs Fire burned 36,807 acres across Sonoma and Napa counties, destroyed 5,636 structures and killed 22 people; Coffey Park lost roughly 1,300 homes in a single night. Wire captions on the frame credit it to Getty Images and AFP staff photographers working over Santa Rosa on October 10-11, 2017. Reverse-image search on the still shows its later circulation runs almost entirely through directed-energy-weapon videos published from 2023 onward, which reuse the 2017 photograph without dating or locating it.

notes: Backstage. ID by Yandex CBIR on the still: exact-size matches include a Malaysian daily captioned 'Coffey Park ... Santa Rosa, California,' a 5065x2758 Independent reproduction credited AFP/Getty, and multiple Greg Reese 'Directed Energy Weapons Burning Homes to Ash' reposts (Rumble/Brighteon, 2023). Credit is pinned to the wire agencies but NOT to a single named photographer — the same aerial run that day produced near-identical frames from Justin Sullivan (Getty) and Elijah Nouvelage (AFP), and the low-resolution repost cannot be assigned to one of them. Claim text says 'Getty and AFP staff photographers' rather than naming one; do not tighten this without pulling the licensed original. Group A on location/event/date. The DEW reading is Group B.
